chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Pops Smith cheating at cards
summary: Pops cheated at cards, hiding cards in the baggage rack, and took Hinton's money on the train.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But one thing I remember about him -- this is not music -- but we used to get into card games and Pops used to cheat, you know, --
He sure did. He beat me.
-- and he'd cheat, you know, and the guys would tell him, "All right, I caught you cheating." He said, "All right, if you want me to quit, I'll quit," but he
had won all the money, you see. He'd have cards on up by the -- standing on the train, you know, --
-- up in the baggage rack. He'd have cards all up in the baggage rack.

I never shall forget what, I think, one of the last times he -- I quit gambling, so I never gambled hardly much since -- he beat me on the train playing poker and I put all my money and I had kings showing and he had kings showing and he had a king-eight high, and where that eight came from I'll never know. But it took every dime I had. I was so sure, I was so sure I had that money that I didn't know what to do. He was really a fantastic man and he really would cheat at cards. Pops used to always cheat.
He was a phenomenal man even though he couldn't read, you know. But play cards, count money? Forget it. He was the champ.
